newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Dec 12.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

English-born Queensland cricketer Andrew Symonds announced yesterday he will be available for selection for Australia rather than England. Symonds, who plays for English county club Gloucestershire, needed to signal his allegiance to Australia after the English Test and County Cricket Board ruled that if he played for Australia A this Friday against the West Indies, he could no longer play for England, and would be classed as an overseas player. Page 22.

The Perth Heat baseball team, which is classed as the Australian Baseball League favourite, is on the market for about A$1.2 million. After eight years, owner Brett Fogarty decided other business interests do not allow him the time for the team, and there was speculation yesterday that at least two groups in Australia were looking to buy ABL franchises. Page 20.

The Kookaburras, the Australian men's hockey team, is out of contention in the Champion Trophy tournament in Madras after losing to Germany 3-1. The Atlanta bronze medal team will play its final matches for pride after it took a largely experimental side to the tournament that left them without experience or combination. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Newly-appointed Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker has taken on probably the worst job in sport, and he did not even apply for it. The former Balmain hooker, current club president and senior executive with a leading public company, is hoping to restore the health of the troubled game and its embattled governing body. Page 48.

Queensland golfer Brad Hughes and Victorian golfer Stuart Appleby have both secured their US$60 million cards to the U.S. golf circuit for 1997. Both players were awarded the cards after torrential rain stopped play in the sixth and final round of the California qualifying school and officials gave cards to the 49 players who were on level par or better after 90 holes. Page 47.

Australian Olympic Committee president John Coates yesterday released details of the A$22 million pool of grants for athletes to prepare for the Sydney 2000 Games. The Medal Incentive Scheme will give quarterly funding to athletes according to their successes in the lead up to the 2000 Games. Page 47.
THE AGE

Pakistan cricket captain Wasim Akram arrived in Australia to prepare for the three-way international limited-overs series against Australia and the West Indies, saying it was a shame the Test series between Australia and the West Indies was being billed as an unofficial battle for the world title, and claiming that players do not try as hard in the one-day form of the game. Page B8.

The interstate war to host golf's President's Cup in 1998 began yesterday, with Melbourne Major Events Company head Ron Walker claiming Sydney's ability to stage international sporting events was inferior to Melbourne's. Walker said that with Melbourne staging events such as the Australian Grand Prix, and next year's Bledisloe Cup, he hoped the President's cup would be next. Page B8.

Victorian Opposition Sport spokesman John Pandazopoulos has spoken out against the involvement of Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett in the Victorian Soccer Federation elections to be held tonight. Pandazopoulos says Kennett's backing of former Socceroo goalkeeper Jack Reilly for the position of chairman establishes a dangerous precedent. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

AFL Players' Association executive director Peter Allen confirmed last night players of the West Bulldogs would be paid in full by the end of next week. The announcement comes as speculation continues over the club losing its banker after many players were asked to accept deferred payments, with a balance being paid in June. Page 112.

Collingwood AFL club captain Gavin Brown has agreed to terms with the Magpies after knocking back an offer from the Melbourne Demons. Collingwood president Kevin Rose announced the re-signing of the three year contract at the club's annual general meeting. Page 110.

The National Australia Bank will sponsor 12 leading Olympic athletes in a unique scheme that will see the athletes involved in marketing the banks' products and services in Australia in return for the National to help them develop individual promotion andbusiness skills. Among the athletes to be sponsored are basketballer Andrew Gaze, pole vaulter Emma George, and swimmer Daniel Kowalski. Page 102.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

As the Australian Olympic Committee yesterday handed out Sydney Olympic training funds to Australia's Atlanta medallists, questions are being raised over whether men's tennis doubles gold medallists Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge, who between them earned A$3,052,723 this year alone, should give their money back to struggling amateurs. Page 104.

Australian triathlete Lena Edmonston is training to regain her place in the elite St George Grand Prix triathlon series beginning in the new year after serving out a five-month ban from the sport as a result of her abusing an official earlier this year. Edmonston will compete in this weekend's St George Australian sprint championships in Melbourne. Page 102.

Former Manly rugby league player Des Hasler has come out of retirement once more to play for Western Suburbs. Hasler, 36, gave up his position in coaching and development with Manly to return to the field, saying he just wants to continue playing rugby league. Page 96.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
